questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *

questions.answer: I wanted to study in spanish and Madrid seemed like a great city to live in

questions.answer: easy enough, the university was always very friendly and eager to help

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
There are plenty of rooms on idealista but its more expensive than i had thought. use idealista or facebook groups and be clear with yourself about what you're searching for. 
also think about how close it is to the university, since the complutense is quite far away i recommend living in the northern part of madrid, moncloa, champeri because the best transport options are from there. but plenty of the neighboorhoods in madrid are nice (just stay away from the center center), i also recommend lavapies, embajadores.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: there are plenty of rooms and you'll find something nice. just be patient. check idealista and facebook and once you get there also talk to your friends and the people you meet, thats how i got my room.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: i dont remember much from this process, i think you just have to show up and get your papers signed, go to the intro meetings and then the classes start and you go to them

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: there is an erasmus office that are very friendly and willing to help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i changed 3 of my classes once i arrived, that went completely fine

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: just contact the erasmus office if you're in doubt

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: there is a big workload in many of the courses, homework, presentations etc. i had trouble finding time for it all so be clever when you sign up for courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: the classes are quite small which is really amazing, you really get to know some of the professers and you can participate a lot if you want to. there are more homework and presentations at the complutense and some of the classes you have to attend and the professer keeps track on that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ANTROPOLOGÍA DEL GÉNERO
TEORIAS ANTROPOLÓGICAS CLÁSICAS
ANTROPOLOGÍA DEL PARENTESCO Y FAMILIA
CONFLICTOS SOCIALES Y VIOLENCIA COLECTIVA
INTRODUCCIÓN A LA ANTROPOLOGÍA SOCIAL

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
CONFLICTOS SOCIALES Y VIOLENCIA COLECTIVA was a really interesting course. the texts we read we really good and the professer Alberto Arribas is completely amazing. We had to do a lot of presentations in the class but in a very casual way, its a good practice and he also lets you do the presentations in english if you prefer that. I really recommend this class

ANTROPOLOGÍA DEL GÉNERO this class was fun, the workload wasnt too high and there is a nice energy in the room. i really recommend. Also really nice professers

ANTROPOLOGÍA DEL PARENTESCO Y FAMILIA - this class was more like the ones im used to in Copenhagen, reading a text or to for every class and then the professor had prepared some really good presentations. The professor Laura Perez Gil is really good, I would recommend going to any of her classes. She is super well prepared, does some really good classes and is super nice. And it was interesting for me to get a better understanding of kinship anthropology

TEORIAS ANTROPOLÓGICAS CLÁSICAS - the professor, Laura Calle Alzate is completely amazing. But I think the workload for this class was a bit too high for my taste. A lot of homework, assigments and debates where you have to attend.

INTRODUCCIÓN A LA ANTROPOLOGÍA SOCIAL - this is is an intro class for the 1st semester students. i really like Pichardo, the teacher, and the vibe is casual and nice. we went to a lot of museums and there was a great atmosphere. I recommend it if you want a more chill class

questions.answer: many clubs and different things

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the sangriada every thursday is nice to connect with the people in your uni

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go hiking, theres nice places close!!! madrid is amazing but its also so nice to escape the hecticality a bit

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: be open and friendly, ask questions, try to do tasks for school with them also. go to the sangriada, go to demonstrations with them

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: it was difficult for me to understand when its appropriate to be late and when not. i think in general things related to time was the most challenging cultural difference

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the openness and friendlyness, tapas culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- enjoy it all, also the difficult parts
- say yes to things/offers even though you feel to tired 
- enjoy the vibe la complu, connect with the students and teachers and remember that the grades dont matter at all

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
i would recommend going to a lot of the erasmus events, i didnt go to many of them because i didnt think they looked nice but i think its an easy way of making friends. i think its a good idea not to be too picky in the beginning. 
the salsa in the retiro park was fun

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: becoming more confident in spanish, making spanish and latin friends and just being able to enjoy madrid lifestyle

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: in the beginning i was really destroyed after some long schooldays, i really had to get used to that and to having classes in spanish. i also started out in an apartment which was too far away from the uni, the long transport times combined with long schooldays wasnt nice - so i moved and im really grateful for that.

questions.question: Any other comments?

questions.answer: Yes
